text: poisoners were, by Act of Parliament, condemned to be boiled to death. This Act was repealed in the following reign. In Germany, even in the seventeenth century, this horrible punishment was inflicted on coiners and counterfeiters. Taylor, the Water Poet, describes an execution he witnessed in Hamburg in 1616. The judgment pronounced against a coiner of false money was that he should ‘be boiled to death in oil; not thrown into the vessel at once, but with a pulley or rope to be hanged under the armpits, and then let down into the oil by degrees; first the feet, and next the legs, and so to boil his flesh from his bones alive.’--Dr. J. Hammond Trumbull’s Blue Laws, True and False, p. 13.
